To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 30 day mortality rate in ARDS is high, that the mortality risk is increased by a longer interval between admission and the development of ARDS, that the mortality is increased if ARDS is caused by direct lung injury, that the risk of mortality is increased with a lower PaO2/FIO2 ratio, and that the mortality rate is lower in patients who receive a lower tidal volume.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Acute Respiratroy Distress Syndrome ( ARDS ) is a severe form of lung injury with a poor prognosis, but that survival is related to the severity of the illness, the type of lung injury, the duration of ARDS and mechanical ventilator settings.
the ARDS cohort studied was representative of ARDS in a university hospital ICU and that the 30-day survival rate of 41% (CI: 33%-50%) was consistent with the literature.
the mortality risk for patients admitted with ARDS to the ICU is high and is influenced by multiple factors including the time from ICU admission to onset of the syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARDS is a dynamic process with a changing risk profile over time, and that ventilator tidal volume is a key determinant of outcome.
